units.t: Conversación: estrategias para hablar con fluidez

learn: Fillers buy thinking time: pues, bueno, a ver, o sea, es que.
Connectors link ideas: además, sin embargo, por eso, en cambio, es decir.
Fluent speakers keep talking by rephrasing instead of stopping.
lessons.try: Talk for two minutes on a random topic without switching to English.

learn: If you forget a word, describe it: "Es una cosa que se usa para...".
Use synonyms and examples.
Ask for help: "¿Cómo se dice...?"
check: "Es una cosa que se usa para..." describes...
lessons.try: Describe ten objects without naming them while a partner guesses.

learn: Show interest: "¿De verdad?", "¡Qué interesante!", "¿Y luego?"
Ask follow-up questions.
Use the right register: tú with friends, usted in formal situations.
lessons.try: Hold a five-minute conversation with follow-up questions.

units.t: El subjuntivo en todas sus formas

learn: The subjunctive follows wishes, emotions, doubt, impersonal expressions and some conjunctions (WEIRDO).
Present, imperfect, present perfect (haya hablado) and pluperfect (hubiera hablado) subjunctive.
The tense of the main clause guides the subjunctive tense.
lessons.try: Write two sentences for each WEIRDO trigger.

learn: Always subjunctive: para que, a menos que, antes de que, sin que, con tal de que.
Future-time conjunctions (cuando, hasta que, en cuanto) take the subjunctive for future events.
Habitual or past events take the indicative: Cuando llego, como.
lessons.try: Complete sentences with cuando + subjunctive or indicative.

learn: Unknown or nonexistent antecedents take the subjunctive: Busco un piso que tenga jardín.
Known antecedents take the indicative: Tengo un piso que tiene jardín.
"No hay nadie que..." always takes the subjunctive.
lessons.try: Write five sentences describing your ideal job.

learn: "En mi opinión", "Desde mi punto de vista", "Estoy convencido de que".
Agree: "Estoy de acuerdo", "Tienes razón". Disagree: "No estoy de acuerdo", "Al contrario".
Soften opinions: "Me parece que", "Puede que".
lessons.try: Give opinions on five statements.

learn: Introducción (tesis), argumentos con pruebas, contraargumentos, conclusión.
Connectors: en primer lugar, además, por otro lado, en conclusión.
Use data and examples as evidence.
lessons.try: Write a five-paragraph argumentative essay in Spanish.

learn: Teams present, rebut and conclude.
Respect turns and speak formally.
Common topics: technology, education, the environment.
lessons.try: Hold a formal class debate in Spanish.

learn: Roman Hispania, Visigoths, and Al-Ándalus (711-1492) shaped Spain.
In 1492 the Catholic Monarchs completed the Reconquista and funded Columbus.
The Civil War (1936-1939) led to Franco's dictatorship until 1975; democracy followed.
check: The Spanish Civil War began in...
lessons.try: Make a timeline of Spanish history in Spanish.

learn: Spain's languages include castellano, catalán, gallego and euskera (Basque).
Euskera is unrelated to any other known language.
Regional languages are co-official in their regions.
lessons.try: Learn greetings in four languages of Spain.

learn: Spain has 17 autonomous communities.
Regional festivals: San Fermín (Pamplona), Las Fallas (Valencia), La Tomatina (Buñol).
Gaudí's architecture defines Barcelona.
lessons.try: Present one Spanish region.

learn: Millions speak Indigenous languages: quechua, guaraní, náhuatl, maya languages.
Guaraní is an official language of Paraguay.
Indigenous movements defend land, language and rights.
check: Quechua was the language of the...
lessons.try: Research an Indigenous people of Latin America.

learn: Millions of enslaved Africans were brought to the Caribbean and South America.
African heritage shaped music, food, religion and language.
Afro-Latino communities are found in Colombia, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Brazil and more.
lessons.try: Research an Afro-Latino tradition.

learn: Rigoberta Menchú won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992.
Writers and artists explore identity, migration and memory.
Latin America has vibrant cities and diverse economies.
check: Rigoberta Menchú won the Nobel ___ Prize.
lessons.try: Present a contemporary Latin American figure.

learn: Horacio Quiroga, Jorge Luis Borges and Julio Cortázar shaped the short story.
Borges's stories explore labyrinths, mirrors and infinity.
Analyse narrator, plot and theme in Spanish.
lessons.try: Analyse a short story in Spanish.

learn: Rubén Darío led Modernismo in the 1890s.
Gabriela Mistral was the first Latin American Nobel laureate in literature (1945).
Poetry analysis: rima, ritmo, imagen, metáfora.
check: Gabriela Mistral won the Nobel in...
lessons.try: Recite and analyse a poem by Darío or Mistral.

learn: Write original stories and poems in Spanish.
Use varied tenses and vivid vocabulary.
Peer review helps improve writing.
check: Stories in the past mix preterite and...
lessons.try: Write an original short story in Spanish.

learn: Mexican muralists Rivera, Orozco and Siqueiros painted public history.
Fernando Botero is known for rounded figures.
Discuss art with "representa", "simboliza", "transmite".
lessons.try: Analyse a mural in Spanish.

learn: Nueva canción used song for social messages (Violeta Parra, Víctor Jara).
Modern Latin music is popular worldwide.
Lyrics can be studied as poetry.
lessons.try: Analyse the lyrics of a song in Spanish.

learn: Directors from Spain, Mexico and Argentina have won major awards.
Film vocabulary: el guion, el rodaje, la escena, el plano.
Write film analyses discussing theme and technique.
lessons.try: Write a film analysis in Spanish.

units.t: Temas actuales: sociedad y medio ambiente

learn: Migration has economic, political and environmental causes.
Vocabulary: emigrar, inmigrar, la frontera, el refugiado, la integración.
Discuss with empathy and multiple perspectives.
lessons.try: Read a migration testimony and respond.

learn: Latin America holds rainforests, glaciers and coral reefs.
Issues: deforestation, mining, water, climate change.
Solutions: conservation, renewable energy, ecotourism.
lessons.try: Propose an environmental solution in Spanish.

learn: Topics: gender equality, Indigenous rights, education access.
Use the subjunctive: "Es necesario que todos tengan..."
Present facts and propose action.
lessons.try: Write an opinion piece in Spanish.

learn: Un currículum (CV) lists experiencia, formación, habilidades e idiomas.
Formal letters begin "Estimado/a" and end "Atentamente".
Bilingual skills are valued in many careers.
lessons.try: Write a CV and cover letter in Spanish.

learn: Use usted and formal vocabulary.
Common questions: "¿Por qué quiere este puesto?", "¿Cuáles son sus fortalezas?"
Prepare answers with examples.
lessons.try: Role-play a job interview in Spanish.

learn: Spanish is used in healthcare, law, education, business and tourism.
Interpreters translate speech; translators translate text.
Professional vocabulary differs by field.
lessons.try: Research a career that uses Spanish.

learn: Review all tenses, the subjunctive, si clauses and reported speech.
Practise with mixed exercises.
Identify your most common errors.
lessons.try: Complete a mixed grammar review.

learn: Choose a topic from the year and research it.
Organise: introduction, three points, conclusion.
Practise pronunciation and timing.
check: A presentation has an introduction, points and a...
lessons.try: Prepare a ten-minute presentation outline.

learn: Speak clearly, make eye contact and use visuals.
Answer audience questions in Spanish.
Reflect on your progress over four years of Spanish.
lessons.try: Deliver a ten-minute presentation in Spanish and write a reflection.
